channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reports that if DT Aaron Donald returns to the Rams, he could play 30-40 snaps in Week 1 against the 49ers.
item.description: For reference, the Rams’ defense averaged 66.9 plays per game last year, so this is a significant snap share estimation. Florio opened the segment by saying, “we could have an announcement within the next few days” about Donald’s potential return. Rams coach Sean McVay joked earlier today that Donald’s recent workout at the team facility was “the best tryout that the Rams have ever seen.” Nothing is guaranteed, but Donald is seemingly headed toward a return.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: FOX Sports’ Eric Williams reports that Chargers WR Tre’ Harris “bulked up this offseason and has looked more explosive.”
item.description: Per Williams, Harris has been a frequent target for QB Justin Herbert. The Chargers’ top-four wide receivers continue to receive positive praise. Although it might be tough for Harris to produce reliably if he is stuck in the WR3 role behind WR1 Ladd McConkey and WR2 Quentin Johnston, he is a worthwhile best ball pick, and he could even warrant matchup-based FLEX consideration in re-draft.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that Chiefs WR Cyrus Allen is “very much part of the offensive plan.”
item.description: According to Breer, Allen “might’ve been the best receiver in camp before bruising his shin.” Internally, the team apparently sees some similarities to Stefon Diggs in Allen’s “physical profile and play style.” Year after year, a Chiefs youngster soars up draftboards after turning in a promising showing in training camp. The results haven’t always matched the hype, though, particularly in recent seasons. Only time will tell if Allen is worthy of the praise he’s received — and only those willing to take the ADP plunge will benefit. He is not without risk, but Allen’s upside is worth chasing.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that Chiefs RB Emmett Johnson “is swiftly earning a role as an explosive, decisive runner.”
item.description: Breer refers to RB Kenneth Walker as an “every-down” player, says RB Brashard Smith “has already shown he can be a weapon in space,” and notes RB Emari Demercado adds depth. Perhaps taking on a change-of-pace rushing role is in play for Johnson this season. The rookie back has pass-catching experience as well, but Smith and Demercado could offer more in that department at the moment. Johnson could be the next player up if Walker were to miss time.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Jaguars signed LB Jahlani Tavai, formerly of the Patriots.
item.description: Tavai totaled 30 tackles and one forced fumble with the Patriots last season. The Jaguars correspondingly waived LB Jared Bartlett.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Cowboys sign TE Zack Kuntz, formerly of the Raiders.
item.description: If Kuntz plays, it will likely be on special teams, but he has not taken a snap since 2024 with the Jets. He is not fantasy-relevant.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill reports that the NFL suspended Saints WR Brock Rechsteiner for the first six games of the 2026 season.
item.description: That is unfortunate. Underhill had previously reported that Rechsteiner was a standout at the Saints’ mandatory minicamp. Perhaps they will keep him around as a practice squad player.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports that Patriots WR Romeo Doubs did not practice on Thursday.
item.description: Doubs was absent yesterday as well. Reiss believes that Doubs’ injury “likely isn’t anything serious,” but notes Doubs “appeared slightly hobbled in recent days.” On Saturday, Patriots on CLNS reporter Tyler Kylesreportedthat Doubs “may have tweaked his ankle.” We are not overly concerned about this. It would be nice to see him return soon, though.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: The Athletic’s Nick Kosmider reports that Broncos WR Courtland Sutton is “being limited as part of the team’s ‘protocols’ for the veteran wide receiver.”
item.description: Sutton did not practice at all over the past two days. He participated in a walkthrough and individual drills today, but sat out team drills. Broncos coach Sean Payton says he is not dealing with an injury, and Sutton said the protocol was set in place due to the fatigue that set in late last year. It sounds like this really is all part of a management plan for the 30-year-old veteran. He warrants FLEX treatment, entering his new role as the Broncos’ WR2.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Lions signed RB Jahmyr Gibbs to a three-year, $67.5 million extension.
item.description: According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the contract could be worth up to $75.75 million and includes $51.5 million guaranteed. The deal averages $22.5 million per year, resetting the running back market. The Lions’ bell cow back enters his age-24 season firmly in play for fantasy football’s overall RB1 spot.-Nic Bodiford
